transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in today because... the thought of getting on an airplane right now just scares me so bad. I mean, I know it doesn't make sense in my head, but my body just tells me that the plane is going to fall right out of the sky. It's just gotten really hard to deal with.
Besides flying, are there other situations or things that make you feel this same kind of intense fear or anxiety?

No, not really. It's... it's just the flying. I mean, I don't have this problem with anything else. Heights are fine, elevators are fine. It's specifically just being on an airplane that does it to me.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F41.1 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder) and F41.9 (Unspecified Anxiety Disorder) because anxiety is specific to flying, not generalized. Ruled out F40.0 (Agoraphobia) because patient denies fear of other situations like heights and elevators. F40.2 (Specific Phobia) is the clear diagnosis - circumscribed fear of airplane flying.

inference_history.note: Patient presents with fear of flying with insight into irrationality. F40.2 (specific phobia) is primary candidate given circumscribed fear object and avoidance behavior. F41.1 (generalized anxiety disorder) possible if worry extends beyond flying. F40.0 (agoraphobia) and F41.9 (unspecified anxiety) included as differential diagnoses pending further assessment of symptom scope, panic attacks, and functional impairment.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a specific, circumscribed fear of flying that is disproportionate to actual danger, causes significant distress, and is recognized as irrational by the patient. The fear is limited to the specific stimulus (airplanes) and does not generalize to related situations (heights, elevators). This presentation is consistent with Specific Phobia, particularly the situational type (F40.2).
